subject: Audit record preservation & export-deliverable details — RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Jane Alvarez <j.alvarez@orchidtx.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@orchidtx.com, Tom Reed <tom.reed@orchidtx.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: RFP sec 4 — logging, retention, exportability clarifications

Ben — thanks for the call earlier. As we finalize section 4 of the RFP, our security team has a couple of clarifying questions on Redwood's capabilities. Could you confirm the following items so we can incorporate them verbatim into the evaluation matrix?

1) Export formats: do you support full audit-log exports in NDJSON, CSV, and a zipped evidence bundle with signed manifest?
2) Export granularity: can Orchid request point-in-time snapshots (for a specified date range) and incremental deltas since last export?
3) Tamper evidence: do exported bundles include cryptographic hashes and a signed manifest we can verify independently?
4) Retention policy enforcement: how are customer retention windows enforced for hosted vs. private deployments (e.g., 7 yrs vs customer-controlled)?
5) Delivery: do you deliver exports to customer S3 (with SSE-KMS) or via encrypted HTTPS transfer?

I attached the RFP excerpt (section 4) with the exact phrasing we want you to respond to. Appreciate a short, bulletized confirmation we can paste into the response.

Best,
Jane
Director, IT Security
Orchid Therapeutics

[Attachment: orchid_rfp_section4_questions.pdf (PDF)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Jane Alvarez <j.alvarez@orchidtx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP sec 4 — logging, retention, exportability clarifications

Jane — thanks for the clear list. Below are the short answers you can paste into the RFP matrix; I copied Marissa (solutions) and Laura (compliance) to add implementation details where useful.

1) Export formats: Yes. Redwood supports full audit-log exports in NDJSON (preferred), CSV (for tabular reporting), and a packaged evidence bundle (.zip) that includes a signed manifest and cryptographic digests for each file.
2) Export granularity: Yes. We provide point-in-time snapshot exports (arbitrary start/end timestamps) and incremental delta exports based on sequence tokens or last-export watermark. Deltas include a manifest mapping to the base snapshot.
3) Tamper evidence: Yes. Every bundle includes SHA-256 hashes for each file and a manifest signed with our export-signing key. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide manifest signing with a customer-provided key (KMS/HSM) as part of the contract.
4) Retention policy enforcement: Hosted (Redwood API): retention windows are enforced by tenant policy in our control plane; deletions are performed by retention-job workflows with cryptographic deletion markers and audit events. Private: retention is customer-controlled and enforced by local policy; we provide the tooling and retention lifecycle jobs. We can document retention windows and deletion attestations for the RFP.
5) Delivery: We support S3 delivery (PUT to customer bucket with SSE-KMS), Azure Blob, and encrypted HTTPS push. S3 delivery includes an integrity check and delivery receipt.

Action: Marissa — can you add 2–3 lines on expected export latency / size limits and a note on pagination for very large ranges? Laura — can you confirm whether we should include a sample attestation language for manifests?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Jane Alvarez <j.alvarez@orchidtx.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP sec 4 — logging, retention, exportability clarifications

Hi all — quick technical addendum you can include in the RFP response:

- Export performance & latency: For hosted tenants, a full 90-day point-in-time export (audit events ~2M records) typically completes within 2–6 hours depending on retention indexing and requested format (NDJSON fastest). For very large archives (multi-100M events), we provide staged exports (split by day/hour) and parallel delivery to S3.
- Size/pagination: Exports are chunked into files sized up to 1 GB compressed (configurable). Each chunk maps to the manifest entry and includes sequence-range metadata.
- Incremental deltas: Deltas are generated from persistent sequence tokens; clients may request since-token X and receive all events up to token Y with guarantee of ordering.
- Access controls: Export requests require a signed, auditable authorization flow (API key + RBAC, or customer-initiated via Console with MFA and approval workflows for Dedicated accounts).

[Attachment: redwood-audit-evidence-sample.zip (ZIP; contains sample-manifest.json, sample-ndjson-logs.ndjson)]

Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jane Alvarez <j.alvarez@orchidtx.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP sec 4 — logging, retention, exportability clarifications

Jane — adding the compliance/attestation language you requested. The text below is intended to be used verbatim in the RFP response if helpful: 

Redwood Inference provides auditable export bundles that include:
- A human-readable manifest (JSON) listing files, sequence ranges, event counts, and SHA-256 digests.
- A signed bundle manifest. For Hosted customers, the manifest is signed by Redwood's export signing key; signature verification instructions are provided. For Dedicated/Private deployments, Redwood can sign manifests with a customer-managed KMS key upon request.
- Chain-of-custody records: every export operation produces an audit event capturing requester identity, timestamp, requested ranges, delivery target, and delivery receipt. These audit events are retained per the customer's retention policy and can be included in the evidence bundle upon request.
- Deletion attestations: when retention windows expire and records are removed, Redwood issues a deletion attestation summarizing the affected sequence ranges and object digests; attestations are available for review and can be appended to a customer's evidence archive.

If you want, we can include a short sample attestation (signed) as an appendix to the RFP. Let me know the level of legal formality required (e.g., notarized, signed statement from Redwoods' CISO) and we'll scope it.

—Laura
Director, Compliance & Risk
Redwood Inference
